subject: Clarifying signatory & billing path after discovery — CloudWorks
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@cloudworks.com>, Rajiv Menon <r.menon@cloudworks.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudworks.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & checklist — signatory path, PO vs card, marketplace interest

Hi Sara / Rajiv — thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the open items we promised to confirm: 

1) Commercial path options you flagged: 
   - Purchase Order (standard SOW + PO) — likely for enterprise procurement team with monthly billing cycle
   - Card (credit card) — for smaller pilots or initial proof-of-value to speed deployment
   - Cloud marketplace (Azure/Marketplace) — interesting if you want procurement via internal marketplace catalog and consolidated billing

2) Internal roles you mentioned on the call: 
   - Economic buyer: Rajiv (CFO) — approves budget commitments >$100k annually
   - Finance sponsor: procurement@cloudworks.com (ops contact) — handles invoicing and PO processing
   - Signatory: likely the VP of IT or Legal depending on contract size / term

3) Key asks / next steps (action items):
   - Ben: share a short checklist that maps PO vs card vs marketplace, and the likely docs procurement will ask for (SOC2, SLAs, MSA draft). Attached.
   - Sara: confirm whether the pilot (up to $15k/mo) needs PO or if card is acceptable to run the 8-week trial.
   - Rajiv: please confirm the approval path and whether a single signatory (VP) can sign pilot agreements or legal needs to review.

I attached a concise checklist that we use to speed procurement handoffs: redwood-commercial-path-checklist.xlsx — it maps typical docs, timeline expectations, and suggested approvers.

If helpful, we can schedule a 20-minute procurement sync with your finance/opps team this week to run through the checklist and avoid surprises — I’m available Wed/Thu mornings PT.

Thanks again —
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachment: redwood-commercial-path-checklist.xlsx (file stub, 42KB)
From: Sara Li <sara.li@cloudworks.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@cloudworks.com>, procurement@cloudworks.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & checklist — signatory path, PO vs card, marketplace interest

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For the pilot (target: 8 weeks, estimated spend ~$12k), procurement prefers to use a card to avoid opening a PO for such a short engagement.
- If we decide to scale to production (multi-quarter commitment), procurement will require a PO and our Legal team will request an MSA. 
- Marketplace: we are evaluating the internal marketplace (we use Azure Marketplace) because it simplifies billing to our central platform and is preferred for SaaS vendors we want on the catalog; however, listing adds ~3–4 weeks.

Rajiv — can you confirm if a VP-level signatory is sufficient for a 6–12 month commitment? If the ask exceeds $100k ARR we likely need CFO+Legal sign-off.

procurement@cloudworks.com — can you confirm the PO intake process and the typical SLA for contract review? Also let us know which SOC2 artifacts you need up front.

Happy to jump on a call with your procurement lead. Wed 10:00am PT / Thu 09:00am PT both work here.

—Sara
Sr Product Manager | CloudWorks Inc.
Sara.Li@cloudworks.com

Sara — perfect, thanks for the signal. Quick answers and suggested path: 

- Pilot: we’ll accept card for the 8-week pilot. To keep procurement comfortable we can provide an abbreviated pilot addendum (one page) that captures scope, expected spend cap ($15k), and basic data handling commitments. That avoids a full MSA for the short term.

- Production: if you move to a committed tier (>3 months or >$25k/month), we recommend PO + MSA. We can pre-share our standard MSA and SOC2 summary to accelerate review.

- Marketplace: if you want consolidated billing via Azure Marketplace we can coordinate with your platform/vendor onboarding team — listing typically takes 3–5 weeks and requires a marketplace reseller agreement. We can run both tracks in parallel if you want to avoid blocking the pilot.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Procurement sync (20 mins) this Thu 09:00am PT — confirm PO intake SLA and required documents.
2) I’ll send the pilot addendum template and the SOC2 summary (one-pager).
3) If Rajiv confirms signatory threshold, we’ll map the exact signatory name(s) and share a flowchart for internal approvals.

I’ve attached the same checklist for convenience. If Thu 09:00am PT works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Ben

Sara / Rajiv — Karthik here (Ben looped me in). Quick note from a commercial perspective: 

- If CloudWorks intends to scale within 6–12 months, we usually align on a PO-based production contract to lock pricing and support SLAs. For pilots we are flexible on card and pilot addendum as Ben suggested.
- If a PO is required and the deal size is >$100k we can route the discount / approvals via our commercial approval path (I’ll own that). For anything under that threshold I can approve standard discounts.

Ben — I’ll be on the procurement sync if that helps speed approvals. Rajiv — if you can indicate the target decision date (e.g., end of Q3), I’ll include that in our internal approval note.

Thanks —
